_meta.authority: CANONICAL for the story-side rules reference shown in the tracker. Read-only in the tracker UI - editable only through the editor.
_meta.excluded: The Explore d20 table is deliberately NOT here. It is GM-narrated; putting outcomes on the player screen pre-reads the gamble.

bands.label: Clean success
bands.detail: You get it, fully and quietly.

bands.label: Success, with a cost
bands.detail: A complication, a price, a hard choice - the most common outcome.

bands.label: Miss - and something changes
bands.detail: Gold lost, a Condition, the Mark. 'Nothing happens' is banned.

storyConstants.circumstances: One die, in or out - never stacks. Favorable: 3d12 keep the highest two. Unfavorable: 3d12 keep the lowest two.
storyConstants.natural13: The result stands, usually still a success - but the old forces take their toll: a Condition or +1 Mark rides in as the cost.
storyConstants.press: On a miss, once, you may reroll both dice. The price: a Condition - or +1 Mark if the scene touched the uncanny.
storyConstants.conditions: A Condition is a named affliction that dims one skill to -3 until tended. They accumulate; a second Condition dims a second skill. A relevant Condition can also make a roll unfavorable. Removed by Rest (2 per camp), Hearty Stew, or certain items.

gains: bargaining with what should not be bargained with +2
mark.lowering: Cleanse only - churches, shrines, festivals, places of power. Never by rest.

standing.gain: deeds only - never bought, never sold
standing.spend: Spend 1 to make a roll favorable, only where another person is the audience or the obstacle. Does not stack with other favorable circumstances.

storyConstants.provisions: 1 per person per dawn. All rations are equal - no conversions. Invited to eat for free: none consumed. Can be bought, sold, and given away.

laws.name: The Clue Law
laws.text: Core information is never behind a roll. Look in the right place, or know the right trade, and you find it. Rolls buy extras - never access.

laws.name: Say Yes or Roll
laws.text: Dice come out only when failure is interesting. Otherwise competence simply works.

laws.name: Let It Ride
laws.text: One roll stands. No retries on the same obstacle, by anyone, until the situation truly changes.

laws.name: Intent & Task
laws.text: Say what you want and how, before the dice. The roll resolves the intent.

laws.name: Track the NPC, never the PC
laws.text: Persuasion moves their meters. No roll ever reads your character's mind.

laws.name: Dread accumulates
laws.text: No depleting sanity meter. The Mark only rises between eruptions. Horror is something you gain.

laws.name: The Firewall
laws.text: Story harm is Conditions and the Mark; combat harm is HP. No system on this side is priced in combat math.

skills.name: Athletics
skills.scope: Labor, climbing, swimming, endurance, the chase.
examples: Hauling the cart out of the ford
Climbing the bell tower by its gutter
Swimming the millpond in your coat
A full night of digging before dawn

skills.name: Composure
skills.scope: Keeping your head: facing fear, steady hands, holding a lie under scrutiny. Trained, you know what frightens people.
examples: Not running when the dogs howl at nothing
Threading the needle while it watches from the corner
Holding your face when the Reeve names you

skills.name: Perception
skills.scope: Noticing, overhearing, reading a room. NEVER ROLLED - the GM simply tells trained characters more, earlier. In negotiation, reads the live signals: what landed, what missed, when you are near something.
examples: The fresh-turned earth by the well
The talk that stops when you enter
Footsteps behind you that stop when yours do

skills.name: Stealth
skills.scope: Moving unseen, hiding, shadowing, the unseen hand.
examples: Crossing the yard between lantern sweeps
Tailing the sexton through market crowds
Palming the letter mid-conversation

skills.name: Survival
skills.scope: Paths, weather, tracking, foraging, shelter, fire.
examples: Reading tomorrow's storm in tonight's sky
Following a three-day trail across the heath
A fire in the rain

skills.name: Medicine
skills.scope: The human body: wounds, sickness, surgery, midwifery, death. Treats the patient - Herbalism makes the treatment.
examples: Setting the shepherd's arm
Telling fever from poisoning
Reading how a man truly died

skills.name: Crafting
examples: The wagon axle mended by torchlight
Fitting a lock, and picking one
Knowing what tool left those marks

skills.name: Scholarship
skills.scope: The written world: reading, letters, ledgers, law, histories, maps, seals.
examples: The debt hidden in the tithe ledger
The precedent that frees a man at the assizes
Whose seal is pressed into that wax

skills.name: Arcana
skills.scope: The magic trade - scrolls, runes, bindings; what is licensed and what is not. Magic that is written, traded, and taxed (Folklore is the magic that never was).
examples: Reading the binding on a contract, not just its law
Knowing which seller's formulae are stolen
What the rune on that boundary stone actually holds

skills.name: Animal Handling
skills.scope: Beasts before you: calming, riding, driving, herding, tending.
examples: Quieting the horses that refuse the bridge
A wagon team through market-day
Knowing the dog is not growling at you
A difficult calving

skills.name: Herbalism & Alchemy
skills.scope: Plants and preparations: remedies, brews, poisons, doses.
examples: A fever-bark tea strong enough to work but not to kill
Wolfsbane recognized in the widow's garden
Knowing what was in the cup by its smell alone

skills.name: Commerce
skills.scope: Haggling, appraisal, markets - finding buyers, sellers, and work. Trained, you know true worth and spot fakes.
examples: Knowing the ledger price before he names it
Finding the man who sells scroll formulae in this town
Spotting the reforged seal on a 'antique'

skills.name: Folklore
skills.scope: The old ways: rites, spirits, superstitions, omens, the songs and tales that remember.
examples: Why the millers salt their thresholds
The right words when a stranger offers bread
The day no one weds on, and why
The ballad that remembers the drowned village

skills.name: Judge of Character
skills.scope: Sizing people up: want, fear, taboo. GROUP CHECK - once per person, one roll, +3 per trained party member. 17+ learn two topics that matter to them; 10-16 learn one; 9- they caught you weighing them and the negotiation opens at -1 Patience. Topics are valence-stripped: you learn WHAT matters, never whether it is a motivation or the pitfall.
examples: What actually matters to the horse-trader before haggling starts
Which of the three brothers truly decides
That the prior fears something more than he wants anything

seamRulings: Perception vs Survival: Perception notices the birds have gone quiet; Survival knows what the silence means.
Medicine vs Herbalism: the body vs the preparation. A poisoning shows both doors - Medicine reads the victim, Herbalism names the cup.
Medicine vs Animal Handling: people vs beasts. The calving belongs to the stable.
Survival vs Animal Handling: wild sign at a distance vs the animal in front of you.

Crafting vs Stealth on a lock: if the obstacle is the mechanism, roll Crafting; if it is being seen, roll Stealth; if both, roll the centre of the intent and let the other side set favorable/unfavorable.
Arcana vs Folklore: written and traded vs unwritten and inherited.
Arcana vs Scholarship: on a magical contract, Scholarship reads the law, Arcana reads the binding.

rules: One action per player per camp.
Rest is the only roll-less action.
Standing may sweeten any person-facing roll.
Cleanse works only at churches, shrines, festivals, and places of power - once per site, per person.

settlement.name: Rest
settlement.outcome: Remove 2 Conditions. A Medicine-trained character also removes 1 from another player.

settlement.name: Steal
settlement.high: 12g or an item of similar worth
settlement.low: Caught - flee with nothing and gain a Condition

settlement.name: Ask Around
settlement.outcome: Rumors, leads, hearsay - contents and quality at GM discretion, informed by the roll.

settlement.name: Craft
settlement.outcome: 2d12 + discipline skill. 10+ the item is made. 9- the batch fails. Rares need a found recipe and roll unfavorable.

settlement.name: Cleanse
settlement.low: The place is silent to you

wilderness.name: Rest
wilderness.outcome: Remove 2 Conditions. A Medicine-trained character also removes 1 from another player.

wilderness.name: Explore
wilderness.outcome: Roll 1d20 - no skill, no modifiers. The wildcard: anything can happen. The GM holds the table.

wilderness.name: Cleanse
wilderness.outcome: Only at a found site - shrine, place of power. As settlement.

negotiation.scope: Named NPCs with real stakes only. Everyday convincing never needs this - Say Yes or Roll.

tracks.interest: Fill it to win them. Each threshold is a better concession - negotiations can partially succeed.
tracks.patience: Every exchange spends 1. Empty means the scene ends; you keep what you earned. Typical 2-4 by temperament.

negotiation.arguments: Appeals, and any skill can carry one: 'the horses are spent' is Animal Handling, the legal angle is Scholarship, the old custom is Folklore. Whoever knows the ground makes the case - there is no talking skill and no single face. Dice enter only when an appeal needs a demonstration.
negotiation.motivationRule: Hitting a motivation raises Interest - no roll needed. Naming the pitfall tanks the scene.
negotiation.lies: Appeals with false content - they work on motivations, and if caught, the claimed ground becomes a pitfall for the rest of the scene.
negotiation.discovery: Judge of Character before the scene, legwork and Ask Around before that, listening during, trained Perception throughout.

theTwelve.pitfall: Scrooge - asks if there are no workhouses; kindness is weakness

theTwelve.drivenBy: Indiana Jones - it belongs in a museum
theTwelve.pitfall: Vernon Dursley - no questions, nothing unusual, ever

theTwelve.drivenBy: William Wallace - dies with the word on his lips
theTwelve.pitfall: Javert - liberty is lawlessness wearing a ribbon

theTwelve.appeal: Profit, gain, the price of things
theTwelve.drivenBy: Smaug - sleeps on it and knows every coin
theTwelve.pitfall: Ned Stark - offer him gold and watch the door close

theTwelve.appeal: The crown, the church, the order above
theTwelve.drivenBy: Brienne of Tarth - the oath outranks the woman
theTwelve.pitfall: Robin Hood - grant the Sheriff legitimacy and lose him

theTwelve.drivenBy: Atticus Finch - defends the case no one else will touch
theTwelve.pitfall: Jaime Lannister - asks by what right the wolf judges the lion

theTwelve.appeal: The name that outlives the man
theTwelve.drivenBy: Achilles - a short life, remembered forever
theTwelve.pitfall: Kylo Ren - let the past die

theTwelve.drivenBy: Bilbo Baggins - adventures make one late for dinner
theTwelve.pitfall: Khal Drogo - walls and treaties are for the weak

theTwelve.drivenBy: Palpatine - everything is proceeding as he has foreseen
theTwelve.pitfall: Faramir - would not take the Ring if it lay by the highway

theTwelve.appeal: Someone kept safe, whatever it costs
theTwelve.drivenBy: Ellen Ripley - goes back for the girl
theTwelve.pitfall: Eowyn - offer her a cage of safety and the scene dies

theTwelve.drivenBy: Falstaff - honor cannot set a leg, but sack fills a belly
theTwelve.pitfall: Stannis Baratheon - grinds his teeth through every toast

theTwelve.drivenBy: Inigo Montoya - has waited his whole life to say the words
theTwelve.pitfall: Luke Skywalker - throws the blade away

economy.anchor: 1 gold = 1 Provision = one person fed for one day

prices.price: 1g - buys and sells at face, the only good with no spread

prices.item: Inn night, bed and board (the meal counts - no Provision consumed)

marketLaws: Everything sells at half price - Provisions excepted.

incomeReference.value: ~4.5g - a living, not the best living
feeds a party of four, alone
15-40g and loot - five to ten times labor

economy.upkeep: A party of four runs 4-8g a day. One specialist earner breaks even for everyone. Adventure is the profit engine.
